analysis.title: Americas Banks: 3Q26 in review; outlook for 4Q26 and beyond
key_insights: Large banks delivered in-line 3Q26 core EPS vs Visible Alpha consensus, ending 18 consecutive quarters of EPS beats. Revenue was in line and margins were about 40bps better, with provisions 8% lower than consensus.

NII outlook is strengthening. Most banks are expected to land at the high end of 2026 NII guidance, and BAC and JPM guided 2027 NII above consensus. GS attributes this to elevated loan growth and continued fixed-rate asset repricing as the long end of the curve steepens.

Large bank loan growth was 7.5% YoY in 3Q26, stable QoQ. C&I grew 12-14% YoY on corporate balance-sheet use to finance AI infrastructure, CRE accelerated to +4% YoY (highest since 1Q24), and consumer loans grew 2% YoY with card improving to +6% YoY.

Top 5 bank balance sheets have grown about 25% since 3Q21, led by MS (>40%) and JPM (>35%). Growth was concentrated in the repo book (28%) and loans (37%), while securities were roughly flat. GS's 2027E hyperscaler capex forecast is $1.2tn, up about 55% since April 2026.
Consensus NII growth is +9% for 2026E and +7% for 2027E, versus 5% and 5% in January 2026.

Deposits grew 8% YoY, driven by 13% corporate deposit growth. Consumer deposits grew 4%. JPM, WFC, C and BAC account for about 55% of industry YoY deposit growth. Loan-to-deposit ratio rose 11pp from the trough to 61% and LCRs are down about 9pp from the 2Q20 peak to 117%.

Deposit yields rose 8bps QoQ in 3Q26 after a Fed Funds rate hike late in the quarter. The cumulative deposit beta of 61% since rates began rising in 2022 is above the 42% historical hiking-cycle average. MS was an outlier in bidding up deposits.

Banks (BAC, C, USB, PNC, JPM, FITB) characterized near-term deposit flight risk from agentic AI cash sorting as minimal, saying rate-sensitive cash has already moved to higher-yielding alternatives. JPM is blocking some outside agents. Banks acknowledged that lower friction and price transparency could raise funding costs over time.

Fintech competition for deposits is rising. Fintechs offer about 4.0% promotional yields versus about 3.5% at large banks and 3.2% at consumer finance firms. Fintech consumer deposit share more than doubled to 1.8% from 0.8% in 2022 and fintechs take 55% of checking account adds (40% in 2022). Five fintechs received OCC charters year to date and five more are pending. XYZ and CHYM have the 4th and 6th largest debit card programs by 2025 spend.

Banks continue to replace securities with loans. Securities as a share of loans fell to about 55%, down about 15pp since 1Q21. Securities duration has risen since 4Q25 to 3.4 years, which GS views as largely rate-driven.

CET1 ratios fell about 20bps QoQ on AOCI losses (the 7Y UST yield rose 89bps in 3Q) and RWA growth. Gross buybacks fell about 33% QoQ. GS expects another 10bps CET1 decline in 4Q26E. Capital markets business leverage (TA/TCE) rose to about 21x from about 15x in 2019.

Capital return paths diverged. JPM gross repurchases fell about 85% QoQ and USB did not commit to restarting buybacks in 4Q26. C and PNC kept buyback run-rates. WFC raised its dividend to $0.50 from $0.45.

GS estimates current large bank excess capital at $64bn (about 80bps above targets including management buffers), rising to $123bn (about 150bps) after Basel 3 Endgame RWA and G-SIB recalibration, then falling to $23bn (about 30bps) by 2029E as higher G-SIB surcharges phase in.

Credit remains benign. Average NCO rate fell 6bps YoY and 3bps QoQ to 0.54%, in line with the 2014-19 average. ACL as a share of loans fell 8bps YoY to 1.7%, so reserves have not kept pace with loan growth. C guided to about 4.0% 2026 card NCL (low end of range), JPM reiterated about 3.2% card NCO, and BAC sees no deterioration into 2027.

Core operating leverage moderated to about 50bps in 3Q26 on weaker fee income, but GS forecasts a 2026E core efficiency ratio of 58%, a decade low versus the 2011-19 average of 64%. Headcount ex-JPM is down 4% since 2Q24.

Trading revenue fell 16% QoQ but rose 11% YoY, with equities trading +33% YoY and FICC -5% YoY as the rate move hurt valuations and client activity. Investment banking rose 7% YoY with advisory +17% and ECM +11%. Most banks expect a seasonal 4Q markets decline, while BAC guided to a smaller drop. GS is constructive on ECM given a strong large-cap IPO pipeline.

Valuation: large bank shares fell 6% since end-2Q26, underperforming the S&P 500 by 9pp, on multiple derating. Banks trade at 60% of the S&P 500 FY+2 P/E versus a 61% historical relationship. P/TBV is about 1.9x 2027E (about 1.7x ex-AOCI), which GS justifies with expected 2027E ROTCE of about 18.5%, about 285bps above the 5-year average.
GS raised 12-month target P/Es by about 0.5x on average, lifting price targets about 4% on average, with 17% average upside and 20% average total return. 2026E-2028E EPS estimates are unchanged.

market_movers.rationale: On the Americas Conviction List. GS sees top-line growth in NII and fees, only modest expense growth and about 390bps of 2026E operating leverage. It expects WFC to reach its 2026 NII target of $50bn. WFC trades at about 10.5x NTM P/E, the 35th percentile of the past decade. PT raised from $94 on a 12.5x target multiple (from 11.5x).

GS sees 2027E NII growth of about 8.5%, about 0.5% above consensus, on asset sensitivity, deposit repricing and fixed-rate asset repricing. Operating leverage of about 270bps in 2027E and upside risk to capital return. Trades at about the 40th percentile NTM P/E.

GS projects ROTCE of about 11.7% in 2026E and 13.4% in 2028E, with a 5% 2026E-28E core revenue CAGR and about 8.5pp core operating leverage in 2026E. Management's 13.1% CET1 target for 2028 is above GS at 12.6%. PT raised from $155.
PT raised from $392 on a 15.0x target P/E (from 14.5x). EPS estimates unchanged. About 19% upside to the 10/28/26 price of $339.30.
PT raised from $200 on a 14.5x target P/E (from 14.0x). 4Q26E EPS raised 5% to $2.94. Risks include higher capital requirements and normalization in trading and IB.
PT raised from $61 on an 11.0x target P/E (from 10.5x). 2027E EPS up 1% and 2028E up 2%. USB did not commit to restarting buybacks in 4Q26.
PT raised from $238 on an 11.5x target P/E (from 11.0x). EPS estimates essentially unchanged.

sector_views.rationale: Constructive on WFC, BAC and C. NII guidance is rising, credit is benign, expense discipline is producing decade-low efficiency ratios, and valuation is at 60% of the S&P 500 P/E. GS sees 17% average upside to price targets.

earnings_insights: Large banks' 3Q26 core EPS was in line with Visible Alpha consensus, ending 18 straight quarters of beats. Median core EPS versus consensus was 0%, median core revenue versus consensus 0%, median core provisions 8% below consensus.
Core EPS vs consensus (3Q26 reported): BAC -4%, C +9%, JPM 0%, MS +4%, PNC 0%, USB +4%, WFC -1%.
3Q26 reported core EPS growth YoY: BAC +3%, C +27%, JPM +14%, MS +10%, PNC +12%, USB +17%, WFC +12%.
3Q26 NIM change QoQ: BAC +8bps, JPM +8bps, USB +5bps, C -11bps, PNC -2bps, WFC flat.

3Q26 capital markets revenue for large banks was $42.2bn (-14% QoQ, +10% YoY). FICC trading $15.8bn (-5% YoY), equities trading $16.2bn (+33% YoY), advisory $3.8bn (+17% YoY), ECM $2.1bn (+11% YoY), DCM $3.7bn (-4% YoY). Source: Visible Alpha consensus and company data.
GS estimates for 2026E: FICC trading +4%, equities trading +37%, advisory +26%, ECM +40%, capital markets +20% YoY.
C has delivered EPS beats in all but 4 quarters over the past decade (peer average 9 misses is stated as the comparison in the report).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hiking resumed in 3Q26 after a cutting cycle from 3Q24 to 2Q26, lifting deposit yields 8bps QoQ.
Drove AOCI losses of about $7bn across large banks, a 0.3pp average CET1 hit, and hurt FICC valuations. Higher long-end rates support fixed-rate asset repricing and NII.
In line with the 2014-19 average of 0.54%. Credit is normalizing, not deteriorating.

macro_indicators.indicator: Large bank ACL as % of loans
macro_indicators.interpretation: Reserves have not kept pace with loan growth, indicating banks are comfortable with reserve levels.
C&I +12-14%, CRE +4%, card +6%. Loan growth underpins NII upgrades.
A decade low versus the 64% average in 2011-19.
About 285bps above the 5-year average, supporting the 1.9x P/TBV multiple.

risk_factors: Rising G-SIB surcharges compress excess capital from $64bn to $23bn by 2029E despite Basel 3 Endgame relief.
Further AOCI losses from rising long-end yields and RWA growth reduce CET1, with another 10bps decline expected in 4Q26E.
Fintech deposit competition and agentic AI could lower friction in moving deposits and raise funding costs over time.
Seasonal decline in 4Q markets revenue, weaker fee income, and FICC sensitivity to rate volatility.
Reserves have not kept pace with loan growth, leaving less cushion if credit deteriorates.

Company-specific: C faces slower revenue growth and higher card losses, BAC less efficiency improvement from NII attrition, WFC slower loan growth or regulatory actions, JPM lower deposit betas and smaller capital distributions, MS higher capital requirements and trading normalization.

vol_and_positioning: Large banks have underperformed the S&P 500 by 9pp since end-2Q26 (shares -6%) on multiple derating.
WFC has underperformed bank peers and the broader market by about 16pp and 23pp YTD, and BAC by 12pp and 21pp YTD, entirely from multiple derating.
Large banks' buyback pace fell 33% QoQ in 3Q26, with JPM down about 85%.

tension_points.bull_case: Regulatory reform (B3E and G-SIB recalibration) lifts excess capital from $64bn to $123bn, and BAC and C are seen with room for capital return upside. C and PNC kept buyback run-rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising G-SIB buffers shrink excess capital to $23bn by 2029E, CET1 fell 20bps in 3Q26, another 10bps decline is expected in 4Q26E, and JPM cut buybacks about 85% QoQ while USB gave no restart commitment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Excess capital compressing to about $23bn (about 30bps) by 2029E as higher G-SIB surcharges phase in, assuming no capital accretion over time.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks say rate-sensitive cash is already sorted into higher-yielding alternatives, remaining balances are sticky operational deposits, and agentic AI deposit flight risk is minimal near term.
tension_points.bear_case: Fintechs offer about 4.0% promotional yields, hold 55% of checking account adds, are gaining bank charters, and lower friction from agentic AI could raise funding costs over time. Cumulative deposit beta of 61% is above past cycles.

theme_stances.key_argument: Loan growth and fixed-rate asset repricing are pushing most banks to the high end of 2026 NII guidance, with BAC and JPM guiding 2027 above consensus.
theme_stances.evidence: NII outlook continues to strengthen with most banks expected to be at the high end

theme_stances.key_argument: Fintechs offer higher promotional rates, are acquiring bank charters and have doubled their share of consumer deposits since 2022.
theme_stances.evidence: Fintechs are increasingly competing for consumer deposits

theme_stances.key_argument: CET1 fell on AOCI and RWA growth, buybacks slowed, and rising G-SIB buffers will shrink excess capital by 2029E.
theme_stances.evidence: capital return strategies diverged across banks
